title: Egg drop soup
summary: Silky ribbons of egg swirl through a light ginger-scented broth with spring onions and white pepper.
method: Slice the ginger and spring onions, keeping the spring onions separate. Beat the eggs in a jug, and mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Put the stock, 250 ml water and ginger in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then simmer gently on medium-low for 8 minutes.
Remove the ginger, then season with the pepper and salt.
Return to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Stir in the cornflour mixture and cook for 1 minute until glossy and slightly thickened.
Reduce to low and swirl the soup. Pour in the eggs in a thin stream, then leave for 30 seconds until the ribbons are set and opaque.
Off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and most of the spring onions. Ladle into bowls and top with the rest.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Thinly slice the ginger and spring onions, keeping the spring onions separate.
Crack the eggs into a jug and beat lightly with a fork until the yolks and whites are just combined.
Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp water in a small bowl until smooth.

stages.title: Infuse the stock
steps: Pour the chicken stock and 250 ml water into a medium saucepan and add the ginger.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Lift out the ginger with a slotted spoon and discard it.
Stir in the black pepper and the salt.

stages.title: Thicken and add the egg
steps: Return the stock to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Stir the cornflour mixture again, then pour it in while stirring, and cook for 1 minute until the soup turns slightly glossy and thickens.
Reduce the heat to low. Stir the soup in one slow circular direction to create a gentle swirl.
Pour the beaten eggs in a thin stream into the moving soup, then stop stirring and leave for 30 seconds until the egg ribbons are set and opaque.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil and most of the spring onions.
Ladle into bowls and scatter over the remaining spring onions.

tips: A thin, slow stream of egg into moving soup makes fine silky ribbons, while pouring it in fast gives clumps.
Keep the soup at a gentle simmer when adding the egg, because a hard boil breaks the egg into small cloudy bits.
The cornflour thickens the broth just enough to suspend the egg, so stir the slurry again right before adding it as it settles quickly.
Add the sesame oil off the heat, as it loses its aroma when cooked.
variations: Add 1 cup of corn kernels with the stock and simmer for 3 minutes for a sweet corn version.
Stir in 100 g of sliced mushrooms with the ginger and simmer until tender for extra body.
storage: Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over low heat until steaming hot, without boiling.

title: Pão de queijo (cheese bread)
summary: Chewy, golden cheese rolls made with tapioca starch and Parmesan, crisp outside and stretchy within.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush a 12-hole mini muffin tin with 1 tsp of the oil and tip the tapioca starch into a large heatproof bowl.
Heat the milk, remaining oil and salt in a small saucepan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until steaming with small bubbles at the edge. Don't let it boil hard.
Pour the hot liquid over the starch and mix until no dry patches remain and it looks shaggy and slightly translucent. Cool for about 10 minutes, until warm to the touch.
Beat in the egg for 2–3 minutes until the dough is smooth and very sticky, then mix in the parmesan until stretchy.
With wet hands, roll the dough into 12 golf-ball-sized balls and place one in each muffin hole.
Bake on the middle shelf for 20–22 minutes, until puffed, deep golden and set. Rest in the tin for 3 minutes, then serve warm.

stages.title: Heat the oven and prepare the tin
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Brush a 12-hole mini muffin tin with 1 tsp of the vegetable oil, keeping the remaining oil for the dough.
Tip the tapioca starch into a large heatproof bowl.

stages.title: Scald the starch
steps: Combine the milk, the remaining vegetable oil and the salt in a small saucepan.
Heat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until steaming and small bubbles form around the edge. Do not let it boil hard.
Pour the hot liquid over the tapioca starch and stir with a wooden spoon until no dry patches remain and the mixture looks shaggy and slightly translucent.

stages.title: Cool and finish the dough
steps: Leave the mixture to cool for about 10 minutes, until warm to the touch rather than hot, so it won't cook the egg.
Add the egg and beat vigorously with the spoon or your hands for 2–3 minutes, until the egg is absorbed and the dough is smooth and very sticky.
Add the parmesan and mix until evenly combined and stretchy.
Wet your hands and roll the dough into 12 balls about the size of a golf ball, then place one in each muffin hole.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Bake on the middle shelf for 20–22 minutes, until puffed, deep golden and set. They should feel light, with a crisp shell and a soft, chewy centre.
Rest in the tin for 3 minutes, then lift out and serve warm.

tips: Letting the scalded mixture cool before adding the egg stops the egg scrambling and keeps the dough smooth.
Finely grated parmesan melts into the dough evenly; coarse shreds leave pockets that leak and brown too fast.
Wet hands stop the sticky dough clinging to your fingers when you roll the balls.
Serve warm, as the centres go dense once cold; a quick re-bake brings back the crisp shell.
variations: Replace half the parmesan with grated mozzarella for a stretchier, milder centre.
Add 1 tsp finely chopped chives or a pinch of chilli flakes to the dough with the cheese.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat on a tray in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 6–8 minutes, until hot and crisp outside. Raw shaped balls can be frozen and baked from frozen for 5–8 minutes longer.

title: Gougères
summary: Airy choux pastry puffs with nutty Gruyère and a delicate crisp shell.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two trays with baking paper. Grate the gruyere, reserving 2 tbsp for the top, and sift the flour.
Bring the water, milk, butter and salt to a rolling boil in a saucepan over medium heat. Off the heat, beat in the flour until smooth and the paste leaves the sides of the pan.
Cook the paste over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until a thin film forms on the base. Cool in a bowl for 5 minutes, until warm.
Beat in the whisked eggs in 3 batches until glossy and the paste falls in a thick ribbon. Stir in the gruyere, nutmeg and black pepper.
Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds onto the trays, 4 cm apart. Sprinkle with the reserved cheese, bake 10 minutes, then at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15–20 minutes, until puffed and deep golden.
Pierce each gougère with a skewer, then dry out in the switched-off oven for 5 minutes. Serve warm.

stages.title: Prepare the trays and cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Finely grate 120 g gruyere, then set aside 2 tbsp of it for sprinkling on top.
Sift the flour onto a sheet of baking paper so it can be tipped into the pan in one go.

stages.title: Cook the choux paste
steps: Combine the water, milk, butter and salt in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring until the butter melts, then bring to a rolling boil.
Remove the pan from the heat and tip in the flour all at once. Beat hard with a wooden spoon until the mixture is smooth and comes away from the sides of the pan.
Return the pan to low heat and stir for 1–2 minutes, until a thin film forms on the base of the pan.
Transfer the paste to a bowl and cool for 5 minutes, until warm but not hot.

stages.title: Beat in the eggs and cheese
steps: Lightly whisk the eggs in a jug. Beat about one-third into the paste until fully combined and glossy.
Add the remaining egg in 2 more batches, beating well each time, until the paste is smooth and falls slowly from the spoon in a thick ribbon. You may not need all the egg.
Stir in the grated gruyere (except the reserved 2 tbsp), the nutmeg and a few grinds of black pepper.

stages.title: Pipe and bake
steps: Spoon the mixture into a piping bag with a 1 cm plain nozzle, or use two spoons. Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds onto the trays, 4 cm apart.
Dab down any peaks with a wet finger, then sprinkle the reserved cheese over the tops.
Bake for 10 minutes without opening the oven door. Reduce the temperature to 180°C (160°C fan) and bake for another 15–20 minutes, until puffed, deep golden and crisp.
Pierce the side of each gougere with a skewer to release steam, then return to the switched-off oven for 5 minutes to dry out. Serve warm.

tips: Beat the eggs in gradually: too much egg makes a loose paste that spreads and won't puff, so stop when it drops slowly from the spoon.
Cooking the paste briefly on the heat dries it out, which gives a crisper shell and a better rise.
Keep the oven door shut for the first 10 minutes, as the steam that lifts the puffs collapses if the oven cools.
Finely grated cheese melts evenly into the paste without blocking the piping nozzle.
variations: Replace the nutmeg with 1 tsp dijon mustard beaten in with the cheese for a sharper flavour.
Use cheddar cheese instead of gruyere and add 1 tbsp chopped chives.
storage: Store cooled gougeres in an airtight container for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat at 180°C (160°C fan) for 5–8 minutes until crisp and hot through.

title: Bakewell tart
summary: Buttery pastry layered with raspberry jam and almond frangipane, finished with flaked almonds.
ingredients: 1 sheet shortcrust pastry (about 25 cm square), thawed
1 cup rice, uncooked, for weighing down the pastry (or baking beads)
method: Press the pastry into a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, prick the base and chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Line the pastry with baking paper and the rice. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the paper and rice, then bake 5 minutes more until pale golden and dry.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 3–4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs and vanilla, then fold in the almond meal and flour.
Spread the jam over the warm case, spoon the frangipane on top and smooth it to the edge. Scatter with the flaked almonds.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 30–35 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean. Foil the edge if it browns too fast.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then remove and dust with the icing sugar.

stages.title: Line the tin and chill
steps: Press the pastry sheet into a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, pushing it into the fluted edge and trimming the excess with a knife.
Prick the base all over with a fork.
Chill the lined tin in the fridge for 30 minutes so the pastry holds its shape.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) while the pastry chills.

stages.title: Blind-bake the case
steps: Line the chilled pastry with baking paper and fill with the uncooked rice.
Bake for 15 minutes, then lift out the paper and rice.
Bake the empty case for a further 5 minutes until pale golden and dry, then cool in the tin for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Make the frangipane
steps: Beat the butter and caster sugar in a bowl with electric beaters for 3–4 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then add the vanilla extract; the mixture may look slightly curdled, which is fine.
Fold in the almond meal and plain flour until just combined.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: Spread the raspberry jam evenly over the base of the warm pastry case.
Spoon the frangipane over the jam and smooth it to the edge, sealing it against the pastry.
Scatter the flaked almonds over the top.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 30–35 minutes until deep golden and set, and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cover the edge with foil if the pastry browns too quickly.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Cool the tart in the tin for 10 minutes so the jam settles and it slices cleanly.
Remove from the tin and dust with the icing sugar before slicing.

tips: Blind-baking until dry keeps the base crisp under the wet jam and frangipane.
Spreading the jam on the warm case helps it go on evenly without tearing the pastry.
Sealing the frangipane against the pastry edge stops jam bubbling up the sides.
Resting the tart before slicing lets the filling firm up so the slices hold together.
variations: Swap the raspberry jam for cherry or apricot jam.
Add 1/2 tsp almond extract to the frangipane for a stronger almond flavour.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

title: Sabudana khichdi
summary: Tender tapioca pearls tossed with cumin, peanuts, potatoes and lime for a lightly spiced breakfast.
ingredients: 1 potato, peeled and cut into 1 cm dice
method: Rinse the sabudana pearls until the water runs almost clear, then soak in 200 ml water for 4 hours until soft. Drain and rest for 15 minutes.
Dice the potato, chop the chilli and coriander, and crush the peanuts. Toss the pearls with the peanuts and salt.
Heat the ghee in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the potato and cook for 8–10 minutes until golden and tender. Stir in the chilli and cook for 1 minute.
Reduce to medium-low, add the pearl mixture and cook for 5–7 minutes until translucent and soft through.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice and check the salt. Scatter with coriander and serve warm.

stages.title: Rinse and soak the sabudana
steps: Rinse the sabudana pearls in a sieve under cold running water for about 1 minute, until the water runs almost clear.
Tip the pearls into a bowl and add 200 ml water, just enough to level with the pearls.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 4 hours, until the pearls are soft and can be squashed easily between two fingers.
Drain in a sieve and leave for 15 minutes so the pearls are dry and separate.

stages.title: Prepare the flavourings
steps: Peel the potato and cut it into 1 cm dice.
Finely chop the green chilli and the coriander.
Coarsely crush the roasted peanuts.
Toss the drained pearls with the crushed peanuts and the salt.

stages.title: Cook the potato and spices
steps: Heat the ghee in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Add the cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds, until they sizzle and smell fragrant.
Add the potato and cook, stirring often, for 8–10 minutes until golden and tender when pierced with a knife.
Stir in the green chilli and cook for 1 minute.

stages.title: Cook the sabudana
steps: Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the pearl and peanut mixture to the pan.
Cook, stirring gently, for 5–7 minutes until the pearls turn translucent and are soft all the way through.
Remove the pan from the heat.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt.
Scatter over the coriander and serve straight away while warm.

tips: Soak the pearls in just enough water rather than a full bowl, as excess water makes them gluey and they clump in the pan.
Rest the drained pearls for 15 minutes so surface moisture dries off, which helps them stay separate when fried.
Cook the potato until tender before adding the pearls, because the pearls need only a short time and won't soften the potato.
Add the lime juice off the heat so it stays fresh and sharp.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp white sugar with the salt for the sweet-sour balance common in Maharashtrian versions.
Replace the potato with 1 small diced sweet potato and cook it until just tender.
storage: Best eaten fresh as the pearls firm up when cold. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in a pan over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot.

title: Sesame balls
summary: Crisp golden glutinous-rice balls coated in sesame seeds with a sweet red-bean centre.
method: Dissolve the sugar in the warm water, then mix it gradually into the glutinous rice flour. Knead 2–3 minutes until smooth and soft, then cover with a damp tea towel.
Roll the red bean paste into 16 small balls of about 10 g. Divide the dough into 16 pieces of about 25 g and flatten each into a disc.
Wrap each disc around a ball of bean paste and pinch to seal. Roll smooth, moisten lightly, then coat evenly in the sesame seeds.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan over medium-low heat to 150–160°C, until a sesame seed sizzles gently without browning.
Fry 5–6 balls at a time for 6–8 minutes, turning, until puffed, floating and golden. Drain, and bring the oil back to temperature between batches.
Rest for 5 minutes, as the filling is very hot. Serve warm while the shells are crisp.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Stir the sugar into 150 ml warm water in a jug until the sugar dissolves completely.
Put the glutinous rice flour in a large bowl and pour in the sugar water a little at a time, mixing with your hand.
Knead for 2–3 minutes until the dough is smooth, soft and no longer sticks to your hands. If it cracks, knead in 1 tsp more water; if it sticks, knead in a little more flour.
Cover the bowl with a damp tea towel so the dough does not dry out.

stages.title: Fill and shape the balls
steps: Divide the red bean paste into 16 portions of about 10 g and roll each into a small ball.
Divide the dough into 16 equal pieces of about 25 g and roll each into a ball.
Flatten one dough ball into a disc about 6 cm wide, place a ball of red bean paste in the centre and fold the dough up around it.
Pinch the edges together to seal with no gaps, then roll between your palms until smooth and round.
Lightly moisten each ball with wet fingers, then roll it in the sesame seeds until evenly coated and press gently so the seeds stick.

stages.title: Fry the sesame balls
steps: Pour the oil into a deep heavy-based saucepan or wok and heat over medium-low heat to 150–160°C. A sesame seed dropped in should sizzle gently, not brown at once.
Fry 5–6 balls at a time, so the oil does not cool, for 6–8 minutes, turning gently with a slotted spoon, until the balls puff, float and are evenly golden brown.
Use the back of the spoon to press each ball very gently against the side of the pan as it fries to help it expand evenly.
Lift out with the slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack or paper towel. Return the oil to 150–160°C between batches.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Rest the sesame balls for 5 minutes, as the red bean filling will be very hot inside.
Serve warm while the shells are crisp and the centres are soft and chewy.

tips: Glutinous rice flour gives the chewy texture, and regular rice flour will not work as a substitute.
Sealing the dough without gaps keeps the filling from bursting out, which would spatter hot oil.
Frying at a gentle 150–160°C lets the balls cook through and expand before the sesame seeds darken. Hotter oil browns the outside while the dough stays dense.
Roll the balls in the seeds while they are still slightly damp so the seeds stick and don't fall off in the oil.
variations: Swap the red bean paste for black sesame paste, or for a filling of 2 tbsp peanut butter mixed with 1 tbsp icing sugar.
Roll the dough balls in desiccated coconut instead of sesame seeds for a milder coating.
storage: Best eaten the day they are fried. Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes until hot through; they will be less crisp.

title: Devilled eggs
summary: Creamy mustard-and-mayo yolk filling piped into tender egg whites with a dusting of paprika.
method: Lower the eggs into boiling water in a saucepan over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolks are cooked through and pale yellow.
Chill the eggs in ice water for 15 minutes, until completely cold. Peel under cold running water and pat dry.
Halve the eggs lengthways. Mash the yolks until fine and crumbly, then stir in the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth and creamy.
Spoon or pipe the filling into the whites. Refrigerate for 10 minutes to firm up.
Dust with the paprika, scatter over the chives and serve.

stages.title: Boil the eggs
steps: Lower the eggs gently into a saucepan of boiling water over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium so the water simmers steadily.
Cook for 10 minutes, until the whites are firm and the yolks are cooked through and pale yellow.
Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with cold water and plenty of ice.

stages.title: Cool and peel
steps: Lift the eggs into the ice water with a slotted spoon and leave for 15 minutes, until completely cold.
Tap each egg all over on the bench, then peel under cold running water so the shell slips off without tearing the whites.
Pat the eggs dry with paper towel.

stages.title: Make the filling
steps: Cut each egg in half lengthways and pop the yolks into a bowl, keeping the whites intact.
Mash the yolks with a fork until fine and crumbly.
Add the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, white vinegar, salt and black pepper and stir until smooth and creamy.
Taste and add a little more salt if needed.

stages.title: Fill and chill
steps: Spoon the filling into the egg whites, or pipe it using a piping bag with a star nozzle for a neater finish.
Refrigerate the eggs, uncovered or loosely covered, for 10 minutes to firm up.
Dust with the paprika, scatter over the chives and serve.

tips: Cooling the eggs in ice water stops the cooking, which prevents a grey-green ring around the yolks and makes the shells easier to peel.
Eggs that are a week or two old peel more cleanly than very fresh ones, so you lose less white.
Mash the yolks to a fine crumb before adding the wet ingredients, because lumps will not smooth out once the mayonnaise goes in.
Wiping the bench and trimming a thin slice off the base of each white stops the eggs sliding around on the platter.
variations: Stir 2 tbsp finely chopped crispy bacon into the filling for a smoky, salty version.
Replace the paprika topping with a pinch of cayenne pepper and a few pickled jalapeno slices for heat.
storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Serve cold and do not reheat.
